reference.source: Kelley & Firestein's Textbook of Rheumatology / EULAR systemic sclerosis guidance
clinicalPearls: Skin thickening extends proximal to the elbows and knees and onto the trunk, often progressing rapidly in the first years
Raynaud phenomenon typically appears close in time to skin change rather than long before it
Anti-topoisomerase I (anti-Scl-70) associates with interstitial lung disease, while anti-RNA polymerase III associates with rapid skin progression and renal crisis
Interstitial lung disease is a leading cause of mortality and warrants early screening and monitoring
The risk of scleroderma renal crisis is highest early in diffuse disease and is increased by glucocorticoid exposure
Tendon friction rubs, arthralgia, and rapidly worsening skin score suggest active, progressive disease
The modified Rodnan skin score is used to track cutaneous extent and disease activity
reference.pathophysiology: Diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis is characterised by widespread immune-driven fibrosis and obliterative vasculopathy. Endothelial injury, T-cell and B-cell activation, and profibrotic mediators including transforming growth factor beta drive fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transformation and excessive collagen deposition across skin and internal organs. Autoantibodies such as anti-topoisomerase I and anti-RNA polymerase III mark distinct clinical phenotypes. Rapidly progressive fibrosis of the lungs produces interstitial disease, while intimal proliferation in renal vessels predisposes to renal crisis.
additionalInvestigations: Antinuclear antibody with anti-Scl-70 and anti-RNA polymerase III testing
High-resolution CT of the chest for interstitial lung disease
Pulmonary function tests including forced vital capacity and diffusing capacity
Transthoracic echocardiography to assess for pulmonary hypertension
Blood pressure and renal function monitoring for early renal crisis
redFlags: Abrupt hypertension with rising creatinine indicating scleroderma renal crisis
Rapidly declining forced vital capacity from progressive interstitial lung disease
New exertional breathlessness suggesting pulmonary hypertension
Fulminant skin progression with tendon friction rubs
reference.prognosis: Diffuse disease carries higher morbidity and mortality than limited disease, driven mainly by interstitial lung disease, pulmonary hypertension, and renal crisis. Skin may stabilise or soften after the early active phase, and early organ-directed therapy improves outcomes.
pitfalls: Using higher-dose glucocorticoids and precipitating scleroderma renal crisis
Delaying lung disease screening until symptoms are advanced
Misreading softening skin as remission while internal organ disease progresses
Failing to recognise anti-RNA polymerase III as a marker of renal crisis risk
references: EULAR recommendations for the treatment of systemic sclerosis
management: Immunosuppression to control rapidly progressive skin and interstitial lung disease with mycophenolate, cyclophosphamide, rituximab or tocilizumab, adding nintedanib for progressive pulmonary fibrosis
Early ACE-inhibitor treatment for scleroderma renal crisis, and avoidance of high-dose corticosteroids given their role in precipitating it
Vasodilators for Raynaud phenomenon and digital ulcers, including calcium channel blockers, phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors and endothelin receptor antagonists
Proton pump inhibitors and prokinetics for oesophageal and gastrointestinal dysmotility
Blood-pressure and renal monitoring, especially early in diffuse disease, alongside pulmonary function and echocardiographic surveillance
Consideration of autologous haematopoietic stem cell transplantation in selected patients with rapidly progressive disease
Multidisciplinary specialist care with physiotherapy for skin and joint contractures
